name: Konijnen
description: Konijnen (Dutch for 'Rabbits') is a fast-paced, family-friendly shedding game popular in the Netherlands and Scandinavia (where it is known as 'Kanin'). The objective is to be the first to empty your hand by playing cards into numerical sequences on the table. It is known for its speed and the 'tactical shifting' rules that allow players to rearrange table piles to fit their cards.

history.origins: Part of the broader European family of 'Solitaire-style' shedding games. It gained popularity in the Netherlands in the mid-20th century as a social game between neighbors.
timeline: 1950s: First variants emerge in Dutch social clubs.
1980s: Standardized rules appear in Dutch family game anthologies.
2010s: Gains a second life as a popular app-based game in Norway (Kanin).
Present: A staple children's and family game in the Benelux region.
history.cultural: The name 'Konijnen' likely refers to the speed of the gameâ€”players must 'hop' their turns quickly or lose their opportunity to play.
history.evolution: The game evolved to allow for the 'Switch' rule, where players can break existing sequences to create new ones, adding a light mathematical challenge.

setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 7 to 10 cards. The remainder forms the draw pile.

rules.objective: Be the first player to discard all your cards by placing them into numerical sequences on the table.
rules.gameplay:
1. Players take turns clockwise.
2. On your turn, you must play as many cards as possible into existing sequences or start new ones.
3. **Starting Sequences**: A new sequence must start with an Ace (1) or a Two (2).
4. **Building**: You can add a card to any sequence if it is exactly one rank higher than the current top card (e.g., a 7 on a 6).
5. **Shifting (Tactical Maneuver)**: Some house rules allow you to 'break' a long sequence (e.g., 1-2-3-4-5) to start a new branch if you have the cards to support both (e.g., moving the 4-5 to a different pile).
6. **Drawing**: If you cannot play at least one card, you must draw one from the stock and your turn ends.
keyRules: New sequences start with Ace or 2 only.
Building: add a card exactly one rank higher than the current top of any sequence.
If you cannot play at least one card, you must draw one from the stock and your turn ends.
First player to empty their hand wins.

strategy.basic: Don't sit on your 2s. Playing a 2 starts a new pile, giving you more 'landing spots' for your other cards. Save your high cards (Kings) for later, as they can only be played on a complete sequence.
strategy.intermediate: Hand Thinning: If you have many cards of different suits but similar ranks (e.g., three 7s), wait until a 6 is played to dump all of them onto various piles at once.
strategy.advanced: Stalling: If you see your opponent has only 1 or 2 cards left, and you are in the lead, avoid starting a new sequence with an Ace. Force them to draw from the stock until they happen to have a card that fits an existing pile.
tips: Watch the table carefully! Sequences move fast and a pile that was a 3 might be a 10 by the time it's your turn again.
If playing with Jokers, use them as wildcards for 2s or Aces to get the game moving.
